Putin proposes summit with Trump and Xi to discuss Ukraine deal, WSJ says

Reuters

19 October, 2026 08:30 am IST

Oct 18 (Reuters) – Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a summit next month with US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping to negotiate an end to the four-year-old Ukraine conflict that would favour Moscow, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the discussions.

The proposed summit comes amid warming ties between Trump and Putin especially after the US President announced a deal to buy Russian diesel and signed an order on Friday waiving key sanctions on Moscow.

Citing a former Russian intelligence officer briefed on the matter, the paper said that Putin’s suggestion came in an October 9 telephone call with Trump that also yielded the diesel deal between the two countries.

Show Full Article

The White House did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment, while the Kremlin could not be immediately reached outside regular business hours. The Russian and Chinese embassies in Washington did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

The Kremlin has suggested holding the trilateral dialogue on the sidelines of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, the WSJ report said, citing people familiar with the discussions. That summit is set to take place on November 18 to 19 in Shenzhen.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed to the Journal that discussions were taking place over a potential meeting.

“There is no clear understanding yet regarding the meeting itself or its potential agenda, although all three parties acknowledge the hypothetical possibility of such a meeting taking place,” he told the Wall Street Journal.

A senior US official told the Journal that Trump had not agreed to such a summit, but he could be receptive to the idea.

Trump’s diesel deal with Putin and the executive order waiving sanctions on Moscow have drawn criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who has warned it would embolden Putin and prolong the war.

(Reporting by Abu Sultan and Akanksha Khushi in Bengaluru; Editing by Clarence Fernandez and Christian Schmollinger)

Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv diverts to Sofia on bomb threat, Sky News says

Reuters

19 October, 2026 06:00 am IST

Facebook

Text Size: A- A+

Oct 18 (Reuters) – An Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv with 57 aboard made an emergency landing in the Bulgarian capital of Sofia after a “bomb threat signal”, Sky news said on Sunday, citing the country’s transport ministry.

Austrian Airlines and the ministry did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

Data from air tracker Flightradar24 showed that an Airbus A320, registered OE-LZE, was set to leave Tel Aviv for Vienna at 6:40 pm but was diverted to Sofia at 9:25 pm.

Show Full Article

There were six crew and 51 passengers on board, Sky added, citing initial details from the ministry.

“During the flight, on the border with Romania, the crew reported a bomb threat signal and decided to land in Sofia extraordinarily,” the ministry said in a statement.

An Air Force fighter accompanied the plane until it landed in Sofia, the ministry added, with the passengers subsequently taken off the aircraft.

(Reporting by Anusha Shah in Bengaluru; Editing by Edmund Klamann and Clarence Fernandez)

Driver released after pickup truck kills 2, injures 10 at Kansas youth soccer game

Reuters

19 October, 2026 05:30 am IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Maria Tsvetkova

NEW YORK, Oct 18 (Reuters) – The woman who was driving a pickup truck that entered a Kansas soccer field during a youth match, killing a man and 6-year-old boy, was released without charges while the investigation continues, authorities said on Sunday.

Investigators interviewed the 34-year-old woman, whom authorities have not publicly identified, and consulted with the Sedgwick County district attorney’s office before releasing her, the Wichita Police Department said in a statement.

Show Full Article

Police said toxicology testing and a mechanical examination of the vehicle were still under way.

The Chevrolet pickup truck had been parked near a soccer field in Wichita on Saturday before entering the pitch during a game and striking multiple people, police said.

Five children ages 5 to 9 and five adults suffered noncritical injuries, police said.

Two children of the driver were inside the truck when the incident occurred and were interviewed, police said. One of the driver’s children was playing on a different soccer field at the complex, according to the police statement.

Wichita police will present an initial review of the case to the district attorney early this week, district attorney’s office spokesperson Lyndsee Stover said in an email.

Police identified those killed in the crash as 6-year-old Cole Adrian and 35-year-old Nicholas Schafer of McPherson, Kansas.

“Our hearts are with the families of Adrian and Nicholas as they face an unimaginable loss. What should have been a day of children playing soccer and families spending time together ended in tragedy,” Wichita Police Chief Joe Sullivan said.

(Reporting by Maria Tsvetkova; Editing by Sergio Non and Cynthia Osterman)
